best.label: The best script a blind search found

numbers.label: People
numbers.moves: Up with jobs, homes and happiness. Down with unemployment and smoke.

numbers.label: Homes
numbers.moves: Up when the mayor builds. Down 1% a year as old homes fall out of use. People fill half the empty homes each year.

numbers.label: Jobs
numbers.moves: Only jobs someone holds pay tax; the workforce is 60% of the people. Up with factories, subsidies and low tax. Down with tax above 15%, services below 20, debt over the credit limit, and once a term a recession takes 10%. Jobs above 1.1× the workforce cannot find staff and leave.

numbers.label: Treasury
numbers.moves: Tax in, upkeep out. Interest on debt at 8%. Below zero: austerity.

numbers.label: Pollution
numbers.moves: Factories emit 2 each, people 1 per 1000. Parks absorb a share, less each.

numbers.label: Happiness
numbers.moves: A target of 45 + 30 × employment + homes ± 3 − 0.35 × pollution − 60 × tax × (1 − services/100) + 0.25 × services − debt interest per head − deficit; mood moves halfway there each year.

numbers.label: Services
numbers.moves: Decays 4 a year unless funded. Faster when the city is broke.

levers.label: Set tax
levers.law: Revenue = rate × filled jobs × 5.5. Business drifts toward jobs × (0.15/rate)^0.3, 10% of the gap a year: at 30% it settles 19% below par, at 40% 26%. Tax hurts mood only as far as services fail to earn it.

levers.label: Build housing
levers.law: 1.5 per unit, lands next year. People move in at half the empty homes a year. Jobs do not follow. This is the trap. Homes also wear out 1% a year.

levers.label: Build factory
levers.law: 300 each, 150 jobs after 2 years, +2 smoke a year, 2 lots. Jobs beyond 1.1× the workforce find no staff and leave.

levers.label: Build park
levers.law: 120 each, lands next year. The first park absorbs 12% of ambient pollution, each next one 80% of the previous. Deliberately 10-50× stronger than real trees (Nowak 2014: under 1%), so a park feels like it does something.

levers.label: Fund transit
levers.law: −1 pollution a year per level. +40 upkeep per level.

levers.label: Fund services
levers.law: +12 points per level. Decays 4 a year regardless.

levers.label: Borrow
levers.law: Cash now, 8% interest a year forever. Refused above 5 years of revenue or 3000, whichever is higher.

info_actions.label: Consult the industrialist
info_actions.law: A real one-year forecast, then a bias: jobs ×1.25, pollution ×0.6. Speaks for the factories.

info_actions.label: Consult the economist
info_actions.law: The same forecast, then: treasury ×1.15, happiness deleted. Speaks for the budget.

info_actions.label: Hold a referendum
info_actions.law: Approval % = happiness + the lever's popularity + noise. Citizens hate taxes, love parks.

info_actions.label: Read last year's report
info_actions.law: Every change last year with the decision that caused it.

recession.text: Once a term, in a year drawn from the seed between 5 and 15, a recession removes 10% of jobs. Every mayor gets one. Resilience is how fast the city climbs back.
